reason: M4 is one half of the PMOS cross-coupled load; if you remove it, the circuit can still function as a differential pair with an active load provided the remaining PMOS device (M3) still supplies a pull-up path. Caveat: this breaks symmetry and reduces differential gain/output swing on the VOUT2 side, and may introduce output offset.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (works but becomes unbalanced; degraded gain/CMRR and asymmetric outputs).

reason: Similarly, M3 can be removed while leaving M4 to provide the pull-up action, so the core NMOS differential pair with tail device still operates. Caveat: only remove one of M3/M4 (not both), otherwise you lose the PMOS load entirely and outputs will not pull up properly.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (still operates but with significant imbalance and reduced differential performance).

reason: Removing one input transistor reduces the circuit to a single-ended common-source stage that still produces an output at VOUT1 using the same tail current source (M1) and load network. Caveat: you lose true differential operation (no differential gain/CMRR), and VOUT2 becomes largely undefined unless otherwise biased/loaded.
impact_estimate: Moderate (core amplification remains on one side, but differential functionality is lost).
